correctness.rationale: Direct face classification gives the join K_{n,n}*Delta_R with exactly n missing d-dimensional facets, d=ell-1>=3. The pair relative cellular complex is concentrated in dimension d; J contractible makes integral reduced H_{d-1}(X)=Z^n with basis of oriented missing-facet boundaries. Attaching d-cells to X produces a contractible space, forcing pi_1(X)=0. Hurewicz and homological Whitehead identify the wedge of n spheres. On every subgroup-fixed complex, only fixed-index branches can appear; the same proof gives its wedge or contractible return simplex. The branch-sphere map is an equivalence on all fixed spaces, hence an S_n-equivalence by equivariant Whitehead, and quotients follow. Relative cellular naturality proves primitive inclusion. The embedded standalone verifier has 36 exact graph-face checks, 24 independent mod-two homology checks and 15 subgroup checks; all pass. No finite experiment substitutes for the infinite proof. The finite-group equivariant Whitehead criterion was independently checked against Wolfgang Lueck, Survey on Classifying Spaces for Families of Subgroups, Theorem 1.6 (arXiv:math/0312378): a G-map of G-CW complexes that induces weak equivalences on every subgroup-fixed space is a G-homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural two-parameter integral equivariant homotopy classification for consistently oriented cycle books with nontriangular pages (the first new geometric regime beyond the published triangle book). The class is topologically nontrivial in arbitrarily large sphere dimensions and arbitrary branch counts, and the entire family of fixed spaces, genuine quotients, unsigned integral homology representations and primitive branch-addition maps are determined; none is merely an isolated table entry. The contractible-join puncture interpretation explains the structure and sharp increase in sphere dimension.
